speaker: Angie Jones
en: And then it got to a point, like, pretty AI fluent company where everyone is comfortable using this, I needed to go really deep on the engineering org. And so that was my home. speaker: Angie Jones
en: We really could do a whole lot more to get to this autonomous engineering org. Right? And so I pretty much drank from the fire hose of like all of the news, all of the releases, everything that's going out. zh: 我们真的可以做更多事情来实现这个自主工程组织。对吧？所以我基本上就像从消防水带里喝所有新闻，所有发布，所有发布的东西。我消费这些，过滤掉很多噪音，然后把有价值的东西带给工程师。所以我会说，我对这个领域了解很多。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: And also at my time at Block, I worked on a protocol. So this was like a cross border money movement protocol. So those who don't know Block, that's the company the finance tech company that houses Square and Cash App. Right? So money is our jam.

speaker: Angie Jones
en: So I worked on this protocol. Never thought I would be a protocol girl, but learned a lot about, like, just kinda open standards and how all of that works as well. speaker: Angie Jones

zh: 所以 MCP 是模型上下文协议。这是智能体用来连接应用程序和工具的东西。对吧？我们在 Block 看到了这一点。Block 的每个人都需要 MCP 服务来连接他们正在使用的任何应用程序。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: And so Anthropic realized, yeah, this probably should live in a neutral home. And so those three companies came together to form the Agentic Foundation under the Linux Foundation. So Linux Foundation has been around for decades. Everyone knows them. And so, yeah, so this is a new foundation.
zh: 所以 Anthropic 意识到，是的，这大概应该存在于一个中立的家园。所以这三家公司走到一起，在 Linux 基金会下成立了智能体基金会。所以 Linux 基金会已经存在了几十年。每个人都知道他们。所以，是的，所以这是一个新的基金会。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: So once we stood this up, me and our head of open source came over to the foundation, and we thought it was so cool, we started working here full time.
zh: 所以一旦我们建立了这个，我和我们的开源负责人来到基金会，我们认为这太酷了，我们开始在这里全职工作。

speaker: Chris Benson
en: I wanna ask about the non developers first. speaker: Angie Jones
en: Yeah, these were two very big and different challenges, right? So one is the whole change management of it all. Like you're essentially asking people to think differently and do their jobs differently. These are experts in their domains, right? Who maybe been doing this a couple of decades and you're like, oh, kind of throw away like your processes and everything, and we want you to do this.
zh: 是的，这是两个非常大且不同的挑战，对吧？所以一个是整体的变化管理。就像你本质上是在要求人们以不同的方式思考和做他们的工作。这些是他们领域的专家，对吧？谁可能已经做了几十年，然后你说，哦，扔掉像你的流程和所有东西，我们希望你做这个。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: Not only that, to your point, resistance, right? Fear, lots of different emotions involved in that. And then the whole technical part of it where, like, these tools, like I said, this was very early on, 2024, 2025. You didn't have these nice desktop application. You had a CLI.
zh: 不仅如此，正如你所说，阻力，对吧？恐惧，涉及很多不同的情绪。然后是整个技术部分，就像，这些工具，正如我所说，这非常早，2024 年，2025 年。你没有这些漂亮的桌面应用程序。你有一个 CLI。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: Right? You were copying JSON to, like, get an MCP server work. Like, this was foreign to folks who, like, don't use these tools every day. So it was a really big job. And so, like, you have to consider all of that.
zh: 对吧？你正在复制 JSON，比如，让 MCP 服务器工作。就像，这对于那些不像每天使用这些工具的人来说是陌生的。所以这是一项非常大的工作。所以，就像，你必须考虑到所有这些。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: It's not just, hey. Let me show you how to use a terminal. Right? It's helping them understand where they still fit into the process. Right?

speaker: Angie Jones
en: With things, it's okay to let that go. Like, you probably should not be doing this anymore because it's not a good use of your time anymore. Right? zh: 随着事情，放手是可以的。就像，你可能不应该再做这个了，因为那不再是你时间的良好利用。对吧？然后还有，我我喜欢说两端都有人。有些人，你知道，他们认为 AI 是有史以来最好的东西，可以做所有事情。

speaker: Angie Jones
en: And there's other people who are like, Oh, AI is stupid. It can't do anything. zh: 还有其他人就像，哦，AI 是愚蠢的。它什么都做不了。我喜欢处于中间地带，你知道，我可以现实地对待它的优势、劣势，我应该用它做什么和我不应该用它做什么。只是以此为先导帮助很大，因为我不是试图让你喝 Kool Aid。对吧？

speaker: Angie Jones
en: I'm saying, hey, here's a different approach that could speed you up. Right? That can also give you access to a lot of stuff that maybe you didn't have before. And that part was the key. So when there's, let's say data, right?
zh: 我是说，嘿，这是一种可以加快你速度的不同方法。对吧？这也可以让你访问很多你可能以前没有的东西。那部分是关键。所以如果有，比如说数据，对吧？

speaker: Angie Jones
en: Everybody needs data, no matter what role you're in. If I say, hey, listen, I can get you access with this agent and be like some MCP server to, let's say, records that are in this database, then you would have had to go to another team, put in a request, and ask for a report, right, and then try to figure that report out yourself. zh: 每个人都需要数据，无论你扮演什么角色。如果我说，嘿，听着，我可以让你通过这个智能体访问，并像一个 MCP 服务器那样，比如说，这个数据库中的记录，那么你就必须去另一个团队，提交请求，并索要报告，对吧，然后试着自己弄清楚那个报告。我可以在几秒钟内为你获取那个数据，这样你就可以去，像，做你最好的工作。所以人们，就像，被这类东西说服了，对吧？所以你一步一步地带他们走，并给他们对他们有意义的东西，这可能不是他们的核心工作，只是让他们可以习惯它，他们可以开始建立一些信任，对吧？

speaker: Angie Jones
en: And then eventually, they start delegating a little bit more and a little bit more until they find that right spot of, okay, I shouldn't delegate this. The AI does not do well. I bet. That part, I'll take. Right?
zh: 然后最终，他们开始委托多一点，再多一点，直到他们找到那个正确的点，好吧，我不应该委托这个。AI 做得不好。我打赌。那部分，我来拿。对吧？

speaker: Angie Jones
en: So that was my my overall approach to it.
zh: 所以那是我的整体方法。
